Scoring rationale: Unstable flow or combustion manifestation with possible surge, thrust loss, shutdown or secondary damage; manifestation is evident but precursors may be incompletely represented in narrative SDR data.
Fan-blade damage can have catastrophic downstream consequences; precursor fatigue or damage may require targeted inspection and may be difficult to identify before manifestation.
Abnormal vibration can indicate rotating-system distress but is generally observable through cockpit indications, monitoring systems or maintenance diagnostics.
Compressor anomalies may cause performance loss, stall or surge, shutdown or secondary damage; underlying conditions may require diagnostics or inspection.
Fuel-delivery component failure may impair thrust availability or dispatch reliability; detection may require pressure or flow indications and troubleshooting.
Fuel leakage is safety-significant because of flammable-fluid exposure, although many leaks are externally observable or inspection-detectable.
Instrumentation or monitoring faults affect system awareness but are often indicated by built-in tests, cockpit messages or maintenance diagnostics.
Cracking indicates structural or material degradation; growth may be hidden, localized or dependent on special inspection access.
Lubrication-pressure anomalies can lead to engine damage but are often indicated by warnings or maintenance indications.
Hot-section distress may produce severe thermal or mechanical damage; direct inspection access is limited and degradation may progress between checks.
Lubrication leakage is operationally important but is often visible or identifiable during servicing or inspection.
Oil-quantity discrepancies are maintenance-significant but are normally detectable through indications, servicing records or routine checks.
An engine shutdown is a serious operational outcome rather than a single causal mechanism; the underlying precursor requires record-level causal coding.
Bearing degradation can produce severe secondary damage and internal progression may be difficult to identify without targeted monitoring or inspection.
Fuel-pressure anomalies may affect delivery or engine response and are normally moderately detectable through pressure indications and troubleshooting.
